key: ask How do I propagate a spider plant from its plantlets?|en

sentences.text: A healthy Spider plant produces baby plantlets on long stems, and these can be rooted in water or soil to grow new plants.
The Spider plant tolerates moderate to low light, though variegation fades and new plantlets form more slowly in dim conditions.
Brown leaf tips are the most common complaint with the Spider plant and usually trace to fluoride, chlorine, or salt buildup in the soil.

key: ask When should I repot my rubber plant and into what size pot?|en

sentences.text: A pot with drainage holes is important for the Rubber plant because the roots will rot in soil that stays saturated.
The Rubber plant is typically repotted every two to three years, or when roots begin circling the pot or emerging from the drainage holes.
When repotting the Rubber plant, choose a container only one size larger to avoid leaving excess wet soil around the roots.

key: ask How often should I water my Monstera deliciosa?|en

sentences.text: Water the Monstera (Monstera deliciosa) when the top 2 to 3 centimeters of soil have dried out, which is often about once every 7 to 10 days in active growth.
In winter the Monstera needs less frequent watering, often only once every 2 to 3 weeks, because growth slows and the soil stays moist longer.
Yellowing leaves on a Monstera (Monstera deliciosa) most commonly point to overwatering or poor drainage, so let the soil dry further before the next watering.
